issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for class Animal: the problem statement UML specifies a two-parameter constructor Animal(String, int) (name and age) (problem_statement.md line 29), but the provided solution implements a single-parameter constructor public Animal(String name) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 6). The template Main.java example also constructs animals using a single String argument (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 9-11). This inconsistency leaves students unsure which constructor signature they must implement and how subclass constructors should call super(...).
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred if age is required): update src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to add a public Animal(String name, int age) constructor, add a private int age field with getter/setter, and update all subclass constructors and the template Main.java examples to pass age. Option B (preferred if age was not intended): update the problem statement/UML to specify a single-parameter constructor Animal(String) and remove the age attribute from the UML and textual description.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for class Animal: the problem statement UML declares an attribute age: int for Animal (problem_statement.md line 28), but the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares only private String name and does not contain a private int age field (see line 4 in the solution). This discrepancy leaves students uncertain whether to implement and initialize an age field and its accessors.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add the missing age field to the implementation (add private int age to src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java, provide getAge()/setAge(int), and update constructors and subclasses to initialize age) or update the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute so the specification matches the provided code and template examples.
